statement.p: Consider the function f:\{1,2,3,4,5\} \to \{1,2,3,4,5\} given by

li.p: Find a n in the domain such that f(n) = 5\text{.}
Find an element n of the domain such that f(n) = n\text{.}
Find an element of the codomain that is not in the range.
f(5) = 2\text{,} since 2 is the number below 5 in the two-line notation.
Such an n is n= 1\text{,} since f(1) = 5\text{.} Note that 1 is above a 5 in the notation.
n = 3 has this property. We say that 3 is a fixed point of f\text{.} Not all functions have such a point.
Such an element is 1 (in fact, that is the only element in the codomain that is not in the range). In other words, 1 is not the image of any element under f\text{;} nothing is sent to 1.
